Neelkanth Mahadev Temple: how to visit & the trek

📅 6 Oct 2026·⏱ 7 min read·By Geetu
Home / Journal / Neelkanth Mahadev

Neelkanth Mahadev is the temple our neighbours walk to. It sits in the forest above us, and on a quiet morning you can hear its bells carry down the valley. Here's how to visit it properly — not as a rushed stop, but the way the hills intend.

Quick facts: Neelkanth Mahadev Temple is ~32 km from Rishikesh by road (about 1.5 hrs through forest), or a 12 km uphill trek from Ram Jhula. From JuneGiri it's just ~7 km. Open roughly 5am–7pm. Go early on a weekday; avoid the Sawan crowds unless that's exactly what you want.

The legend

Neelkanth means "blue throat." The temple marks the spot where, in the story of the churning of the ocean, Lord Shiva drank the poison that emerged — holding it in his throat to save the world, which turned it blue. It's one of the most revered Shiva shrines in the region, set where three valleys and two rivers meet.

How to get there

  • By road from Rishikesh: ~32 km, about 1.5 hours on a winding forest road. Shared jeeps and taxis run from Ram Jhula.
  • The trek: a ~12 km uphill forest trail from Ram Jhula — 4–5 hours up. Beautiful, shaded, and the traditional pilgrim route.
  • From JuneGiri: only ~7 km. Many of our guests visit at sunrise and are back for breakfast.

Timings & when to go

The temple is usually open 5:00 am–7:00 pm with an afternoon break. For calm darshan, come early on a weekday. During the Sawan month (July–August) and on Maha Shivratri, hundreds of thousands of kanwar pilgrims arrive — an extraordinary sight, but not a quiet one. October to March is the gentlest weather for the drive or trek.

What to carry

  • Modest clothing and easily removable shoes (you'll go barefoot inside).
  • Water and a light snack if you're trekking.
  • Cash for offerings and the odd chai stall; cards aren't reliable up here.

Make a morning of it

Our favourite plan: leave the farm before sunrise, reach Neelkanth as it opens, sit for a while before the day fills up, then walk a little of the forest trail on the way back. If you'd rather trek the full route or combine it with other hikes, see our Himalayan treks and yatra pages — and we're always happy to arrange a guide.

Some places you visit. Neelkanth is one you listen to — best done before the day gets loud.
